verificationSummary: Editor commit 3b592b48765337efdbd6da539130d2daae1349bc adds a bounded live Backend rich-inline mutation harness. The implementation adds runBackendRichInlineMutation in src/editor/backend/backendMutationRunner.ts and extends src/tests/liveCompatibilityHarness.test.ts so the live loopback Backend path reads capabilities and a Core fixture-backed document, migrates to v4, commits a node.reorder mutation, commits a text-block.rich-inline.replace mutation, applies the returned Core-backed mutation result through Editor runtime state, verifies the updated title text, and verifies stale replay is blocked with blocked-stale/base-revision-mismatch. Focused RED failed after test setup correction because runBackendRichInlineMutation was not a function; the focused test then passed with npx vitest run src/tests/liveCompatibilityHarness.test.ts: 1 test passed. Editor worktree npm run check passed type-check, 90 test files with 313 tests, and build; merged Editor main npm run check passed the same gate. During cleanup, deleting the external sibling Editor worktree caused Core tracked deletions under packages/text-engine-rust-wasm through npm file-dependency links; the Core path was restored from HEAD, Core status returned clean, and Core npm run check passed 460 test files with 2,945 tests. This evidence supports only the bounded Editor live Backend rich-inline harness claim; it does not enable WYSIWYG or text input UI, does not prove broad frontend readiness, production Backend readiness, deployed compatibility, broad corpus coverage, accessibility, visual regression, performance readiness, Core truth, Backend truth, Editor truth, FlowDoc product truth, or map truth. Editor npm install reported existing high-severity audit findings and Vite retained the existing chunk-size warning; neither was remediated in this lane.
